title: Two Londoners share a hair count

probes.question: Ten pigeons are put into nine holes. What does the pigeonhole principle say?
options: At least one hole has more than one pigeon
Every hole holds exactly one pigeon
No hole holds more than one pigeon

probes.question: True or false: the pigeonhole principle says that, with more items than containers, some container holds more than one item.

image.alt: A grey pigeon standing in a square hole in a peeling yellow wall

body.claim: If n items are put into m containers, with n > m, then at least one container must contain more than one item.
body.why: For example, a typical human head has an average of around 150,000 hairs, so it is reasonable to assume (as an upper bound) that no one has more than 1,000,000 hairs. There are more than 1,000,000 people in London, so at least two people in London must have the same number of hairs on their heads.
